author: independent Spring Boot 4 / Java 25 / Python / FastAPI SME critic (Claude subagent, not an item author; Final Assessment coding challenges review 2026-11-19, runs on copies; transcribed from critics/coding-challenges-sme)

findings.claim: [all four (cross-cutting)] The 70% per-question pass mark sits on coarse check counts, so many author-designated WRONG solutions still PASS the graded question. The checks discriminate at check level, but pass/fail does not. Python-2: 11 of 19 wrong variants pass, including wrong-01 (leaks reason + customer_email, 8/9), wrong-16 unscoped refunded total and wrong-17 refuses only 'authorized' (the two loop-0 SME HIGH false passes, which HANDOFF calls 'closed', both 8/9). My V3 (PII leak + timeout mapped to 502, two defects) scores 7/9 = pass. Python-1: 6 of 16 wrong pass (e.g. wrong-02 raw['txn_id'] KeyError 5/7, wrong-06 loops twice 5/7). Spring-10: 3 of 8 pass (N2, N5, N6) plus my X1 and X3. Spring-20 is the opposite: every recorded score is 0, 2, 4 or 6 of 6, so 70% means 6/6. Critic evidence: Recomputed from _private-reference/python-{1,2}/variants/expect.json; I re-ran both matrices with run-py.sh (0 mismatches). New variants: work/variants/p2/V2-leak-pii 8/9, V3-leak-pii-and-timeout-502 7/9. Spring matrices in */README.md 'Scoring at 70%'.
findings.recommendation: Owner decision, made once for all four. Recommended: name 1-2 gate checks per question that must pass (P2: check1 response fields plus check6/7 business rules; P1: check5/6; S10: check4), or weight checks by objective. Otherwise accept partial credit explicitly, and stop calling a false pass 'closed' when it still passes the question.

findings.claim: [spring-10min] ProblemDetail itself is checked in only one place: the content-type assertion in check 4. An advice that returns a plain Map/JSON body {title,status,detail} with 404 (no ProblemDetail at all) scores 4/5, which passes. With N6 (no advice, built in the controller) also passing 4/5, a learner can pass while missing either claimed objective (global-error-handling#o1 or problemdetail#o1). Critic evidence: work/variants/s10/X1-map-body: 4/5, fails only task1AnUnknownIdIsA404ProblemDetail ('Content type [application/json] is not compatible with [application/problem+json]').
findings.recommendation: Also assert contentTypeCompatibleWith(APPLICATION_PROBLEM_JSON) and $.instance == '/api/tools/77' in check 5 (ProblemDetail fills in instance; a hand-built Map does not). X1 then fails 2 checks (3/5).

findings.claim: [spring-10min] An over-broad @ExceptionHandler(Exception.class) that maps every exception to 404 'Tool not found' scores 5/5. The global-error-handling page teaches mapping a specific custom exception, and a catch-all that turns every bug into 'Tool not found' is a classic wrong pattern. Critic evidence: work/variants/s10/X3-catch-all-exception: 5/5.
findings.recommendation: Add one assertion: GET /api/tools/abc (type mismatch) must not answer 'Tool not found' (Spring answers 400). This needs no new learner work.

findings.claim: [spring-10min and spring-20min] Cross-question leakage. The 20-min repo's PROVIDED ApiErrors is a near-verbatim template of the 10-min answer: @RestControllerAdvice, @ExceptionHandler(XNotFoundException.class) returning ProblemDetail.forStatusAndDetail(NOT_FOUND, e.getMessage()) plus setTitle("... not found"). If both repos are released together on the final day, the 10-min error-handling part can be copied across. Critic evidence: Compare with private/reference ApiErrors.java of spring-10min: the same three calls.
findings.recommendation: Release the 20-min repo only after the 10-min one is submitted. If that is impossible, express the 20-min handlers differently (e.g. a single ErrorResponseException-based mapping), or confirm that the final is open-book, in which case this is moot.

location.selector: Test section: 'One run takes about half a minute or more' (Spring 10 and Spring 20 READMEs)

findings.claim: [spring-10min and spring-20min] Time risk against the cap. Every mvn test run in this review took 79-98 s wall, measured on a loaded host (load avg 67-105). The authors measured 50-84 s. On the 10-minute question, the README's expected 3 runs could take 25-45% of the timed minutes, and the 'half a minute' wording undersells it. Nobody has measured a run on the Exa template. Critic evidence: work/spring-results.txt: s10 starter 90 s, reference 88 s, variants 79-92 s; s20 starter 86 s, reference 98 s. `uptime` load averages 66.83 94.71 105.19.
findings.recommendation: Time one run on the Exa Java template before release. If a run is over about 30 s, raise the 10-min cap (12-15 min) or reword the README to say 'up to a minute or two', and tell learners to run once at the end. Note: -Xshare:off in the surefire argLine disables CDS and adds a little JVM start time, and nothing in these tests needs dynamic agents.

location.selector: originally */repo/.evolv/grade.yml test.command (grade.yml is added at publish, not part of the landed bundle)

findings.claim: [all four (cross-cutting)] The graded repos ship the oracle in learner-writable paths (tests/, starter/pom.xml with testSourceDirectory ../tests). Nothing in grade.yml restores the authoritative tests or pom before running. A learner can edit test_main.py or ToolLookupTest.java, or add <skipTests> to the pom, and the Spring run then exits 0 with no reports. The READMEs only ask learners to leave these files alone. Critic evidence: grade.yml runs `mvn -q -B -o -f starter/pom.xml test` or `python -m pytest -q ...` against whatever is in the learner repo. Python-2's HANDOFF already notes that the public tests can be special-cased.
findings.recommendation: Confirm that Exa overwrites tests/ and starter/pom.xml (and Python conftest/pytest config) from the authoritative copy at grade time, or add a setup step that does. Treat a missing or empty surefire report as 0.

findings.claim: [python-1, python-2, spring-10min] The learner-facing labels are stale or inconsistent. The Python titles say 'Python checkpoint question (basic/intermediate)' while the Spring titles say 'Spring final assessment'. Python-2's title never says FastAPI. The Spring-10 test Javadoc says 'Spring checkpoint question I'. Timing wording also differs: P1 and S10 say 'including reading', P2 says '20 minutes of coding'. Python version guidance differs too: P1 says exactly 3.12, P2 says '3.12 or later', and grade.yml says 3.12. Both references pass on 3.14.6 with the pins, so this is wording only. Critic evidence: grep 'checkpoint' over repo/ trees. venv314 run: p1 reference 7/7, p2 reference 9/9.
findings.recommendation: Retitle all four 'Final assessment, coding question N (Python | Python/FastAPI | Spring)'. Use one timing sentence and one Python version statement.

findings.claim: [spring-20min] There is a cliff with only one signal. The README's literal steps without @Transactional (N1) score 0/6: findBySku returns a detached Product, so reserve() never persists. The first failure the learner sees is 'a placed order must reserve its stock', which points toward adding products.save (N2, 2/6) rather than toward a transaction. Dirty checking is taught (spring-data-jpa/seeing-the-generated-sql), so the question is in scope. But on a 20-min clock with 80-100 s runs, a learner who misdiagnoses this gets about 2 attempts. Critic evidence: README 'Scoring' table: N1 0/6, N2 2/6. Taught: seeing-the-generated-sql artifact.md line 35 (dirty checking at flush).
findings.recommendation: Optional: make the happy-path stock assertion message say 'stock changes must be saved; all writes of one order belong together', or accept the cliff as intended. No oracle change needed.
